name: tracker-readonly-db
goal: A native Tracker node refuses to start on a database file its owner cannot write, instead of starting and answering every write with HTTP 500 and no log (found in the ente8j cutover rehearsal)

evidence: Failing: a native Tracker node started on an initialized journal whose file mode lacks owner write (0400) starts, opens SQLite read-only, and answers every write (CLI add, hub /sync/push) with HTTP 500, logging nothing. Expected: startup refuses with exit 1 and a clear reason, leaving the journal untouched. Reproduction: ente8j rehearsal run-185/sbs/attempt1 (cp kept 0400 from candidate.sqlite; lsof showed fd 10r; legacy spokes logged 'hub HTTP 500'); e2e test 'startup refuses a journal its owner cannot write instead of serving failed writes'.

test/tracker-node.e2e.test.ts covered unfenced role, competing API/sync/journal owners and lease release, but only with writable fresh fixtures; a fresh 0400 journal already fails at schema init with a generic message, so the gap was an INITIALIZED journal that later loses write permission (restore/copy from a 0400 backup). Reusable change: the startup-refusal test now initializes the journal through a normal start/stop before chmod 0400, asserts exit 1, the printed reason, and byte-identical journal.

loop record --phase red at 6bfa33aa6b: 'bunx vitest run test/tracker-node.e2e.test.ts -t journal its owner cannot write' failed with 'expected null to be 1' (node kept serving the read-only journal until the 8s kill).
